text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Node group us-west-2-gpu-2 experiencing repeated ephemeral-storage evictions. 17 pods evicted in the last 6m, several are serve-runtime+gpu. Auto-pager to david.pager. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/evict-1919004321


David.pager: on it. Paging now. Anyone oncall for serve-runtime?


Alice_oncall: i am. grabbing context — which clusters/nodes?


Incident-bot: summary: nodes usw2-gpu-12/13/14 hitting tmpfs and /var/lib/kubelet/pods pressure, kubelet evicting pods with ephemeral-storage usage > 90%. Affected: model-cache containers & runtime logs. Error seen in logs: "failed to allocate cache: no space left on device" and periodic CUDA driver warnings during restart.


Carla_runtime: seeing repeated container restarts, stack traces include OOM-ish messages and sometimes "cudaInit failed: unknown error" after restart. Model cache writes ~3.2GB per model load, and log rotation isn't keeping up.


Ben_infra: nodes are 1TB local-ssd, but tmpfs /run and /dev/shm default small. Something is writing lots of temp files (likely model shards + runtime tmp files). I see disk pressure events: 1919004308: node-usw2-gpu-12 DiskPressure; 1919004315: node-usw2-gpu-13 DiskPressure.


Alice_oncall: customer impact? which services returning 5xx or timeouts?


Carla_runtime: partial: 3 model-serving deployments show 5xx spikes and increased p99 latency. Some requests end up as 502 because container died mid-request. No data exfil. Affected customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants in US-WEST.


David.pager: tagging SRE lead @ben_infra for infra actions, @carla_runtime for runtime mitigation. I'm going to start coordination thread here.


Ben_infra: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce log volume from runtime (set LOG_LEVEL=error) 2) rotate and compress old logs on affected nodes 3) cordon + drain most impacted node (usw2-gpu-13) to reduce churn 4) increase node pool ephemeral storage if possible or scale up a new node pool with larger tmpfs. Doing 1-3 now.


Carla_runtime: I'll push a quick env change for LOG_LEVEL and disable detailed request tracing on the hot deployments. Pushing canary to 2 pods then rollout. Also will enable prefix KV-cache warmup to avoid reloading huge shards concurrently.


Alice_oncall: commands pls for ops.


Ben_infra: commands:

kubectl -n redwood-system get nodes -o wide | grep usw2-gpu
# check events
kubectl describe node usw2-gpu-13 | egrep "DiskPressure|Evicted" -A3
# find big files on node (ssh required)
ssh root@usw2-gpu-13 'sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/* | sort -hr | head -n 30'


Carla_runtime: reducing log level now: patch deployment serve-runtime-hot 

kubectl -n serving set env deploy/serve-runtime-hot LOG_LEVEL=error --record

# also disabling request-trace flag
kubectl -n serving set env deploy/serve-runtime-hot RUNTIME_TRACE=false


Alice_oncall: ack. Rolling. Keep one pod at higher level for debugging.


Ben_infra: rotated logs on usw2-gpu-12 and 13: removed old /var/log/serve-runtime/*.log.gz.old (approx 120GB freed across nodes).


Ops-bot: action note: freed 120GB on usw2-gpu-12/13.


Carla_runtime: good signal: p99 dropped slightly, but churn still happening because model cache reloads spike writes to tmp. I'll patch runtime to use STREAM_CACHE=true for now (writes smaller temp files).


Ben_infra: cordoning node usw2-gpu-13 and draining non-critical pods (model-cache pods are high-priority, so they stayed; but we evicted some lower-priority jobs). Command:

kubectl cordon usw2-gpu-13
kubectl drain usw2-gpu-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60


Alice_oncall: is it safe to restart the remaining runtime pods on that node?


Carla_runtime: plan: restart model-cache container after we remove corrupted temp shards. Steps: exec into pod, check /tmp and /cache, remove partial .part files, then restart container. Will do on one replica first.


Carla_runtime: exec snippet:

kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/serve-runtime-hot-0 -- bash -c 'ls -lah /tmp | head; rm -f /tmp/model-shard-*.part; systemctl restart serve-runtime || kill 1 && echo restarted'


David.pager: any CUDA errors after restart?


Carla_runtime: we saw one "CUDA out of memory" during reload correlated with heavy writes; after log-level change and partial cache warmup it stopped. No driver crash. If we keep reloading many shards concurrently we hit OOM.


Ben_infra: medium-term fix: create dedicated persistent volume for model-cache on nodes (local SSD reserved) and mount to pods, or use a shared PVC-backed cache. Raising follow-up ticket to provision node pool with dedicated 500GB tmpfs for GPU nodes.


Alice_oncall: customer comms? any customers need notification?


Carla_runtime: contacting impacted tenants with degraded perf note. No data loss. ETA for full recovery ~25-35m assuming drains and restarts finish.


David.pager: writing initial incident note: impact: degraded latency + 5xx for subset of customers in us-west for ~40m window. Root cause: ephemeral storage pressure (tmpfs & kubelet eviction) due to model cache + log bloat; contributing factor: concurrent cache reloads and high debug logging.


Ben_infra: follow-ups assigned: INFRA-1234 reserve local SSD for model-cache; INFRA-1235 scale nodepool; SRE-5678 add eviction alert tuning.


Alice_oncall: handing off to next oncall in 40m. I'll stay until stabilization and then update postmortem stub.


Ops-bot: stabilization note: after log throttling + node drain + manual cleanup, eviction events stopped. 0 evictions in last 10m. p99 latency returned near baseline.


Carla_runtime: patch to runtime to serialize shard loads is in CI, rolling after smoke test.


David.pager: good job everyone. next steps: document the temporary mitigations in runbook, create follow-up tasks, and schedule retro. I'll update the incident ticket and notify customers. handing back to alice_oncall until handoff time. :thumbsup:


Alice_oncall: handing to oncall-next at 1919008000; will add notes to incident ticket and assign follow-ups. closing Slack coordination thread.


Incident-bot: incident closed for now by david.pager at 1919004610. Follow-up: postmortem required.
